core_principle: Trade reversals after a stop-hunt beyond a key session high/low where price REJECTS the level (fails acceptance). This is a short-window event trade: quality decays quickly as time passes.
event_requirements: Sweep should be relatively fresh: prefer sweepBarsAgo <= 6 (within ~30 minutes).
Sweep intensity should dominate breakout intensity: |sweepScore| should be meaningfully larger than |breakoutScore|.
acceptance_logic: acceptanceTime should remain low for a valid reversal (prefer < 0.4).
If acceptanceTime is high, treat it as continuation risk and reduce confidence sharply.
Best setups show immediate rejection (acceptanceTime near 0).
timing_preferences: Most effective during NY session (14:30–17:30 Zurich time), especially London-NY overlap.
Second best: late London (11:30–13:30 Zurich) if liquidity has built up.
Avoid Asia unless sweepScore is extreme and rejection is immediate.
regime_preferences: Best in RANGE or weak TREND environments.
Avoid strong EXPANSION continuation regimes unless rejection is extremely clear.
structure_considerations: Structure may be TREND or RANGE.
If reversal is counter-trend (structureState opposes the reversal direction), require stronger sweepScore and lower acceptanceTime.
If structure strongly supports continuation in the opposite direction, reduce risk.
entry_logic: Trade opposite to the sweep direction (bearish sweep -> short, bullish sweep -> long).
Entry quality increases when price is still near the swept level (not already far away).
Do not treat old sweeps as signals; the edge is in the immediate rejection.
stop_loss_guidelines: Stop must be beyond the sweep extreme (not inside the wick).
Minimum stop distance must be at least 0.8 × ATR_5m to avoid noise stopouts.
If ATR_5m is very low, widen stop slightly rather than using micro-stops.
take_profit_guidelines: Primary target is mean reversion toward session interior (mid-range or prior equilibrium).
If rejection is strong and structure supports the reversal, target can extend toward the opposite liquidity boundary.
risk_management: High-quality setup (|sweepScore| > 0.8 AND acceptanceTime < 0.2 AND sweepBarsAgo <= 3): risk 0.6–0.8.
Moderate-quality setup (|sweepScore| 0.6–0.8 AND acceptanceTime < 0.4 AND sweepBarsAgo <= 6): risk 0.4–0.6.
Low-quality setup (older sweep, weaker score, or counter-trend): risk 0.2–0.4.
Risk scales with freshness + rejection quality, not a fixed default.
probabilistic_note: This strategy is event-driven. The closer you are to the sweep event and the clearer the rejection (low acceptance), the higher the probability. Old sweeps or accepted levels lose edge quickly.
